blocks.text: Public members are shown by default. Include internal and protected members when exploring implementation details. A direct member link reveals and opens its target automatically, even when it is internal. Large types are grouped by behavior.

Start with the class or option type you need, then open a member to see its signature, arguments, defaults and return type. Use Find a member to narrow the list. Type names link to their own references, inherited members link to their base class, and Read implementation opens the checked-out source directly on this page.

The reference follows the TypeScript implementation, including constructor overloads and accessors. Where a live scene is available, run it beside the contract and use View source to experiment. The workflow links connect individual APIs to the guides that explain how to use them together.

Protected members support extensions; members marked internal expose engine machinery and are best understood alongside the rendering guides. Source comments and authored notes explain behavior where available. The collapsed declaration snapshot retains the earlier implementation inventory. See [current behavior and limitations](/limitations) for known differences between older comments and runtime behavior.
